short: He delivered Brexit, won a landslide, and fell over parties held in lockdown.
full:
Boris Johnson, a journalist and former Mayor of London who had fronted the Leave campaign, became prime minister in July 2019. He suspended Parliament for five weeks that autumn, a prorogation the Supreme Court unanimously ruled unlawful, renegotiated the withdrawal agreement with a Northern Ireland protocol replacing the backstop, and won a majority of eighty in December 2019 by taking traditionally Labour seats across the Midlands and the north.

Britain left the European Union on 31 January 2020. Six weeks later he ordered the first Covid lockdown, was himself moved to intensive care in April, and oversaw a vaccination programme that ran ahead of the rest of Europe. Revelations that Downing Street staff had held gatherings during the restrictions produced police fines, one of them his own, and a Commons committee later found he had misled Parliament. Fifty-seven ministers resigned within three days in July 2022.
